nodes.Name: FuncMap
nodes.DocComment:
FuncMap is the type of the map defining the mapping from names to functions.
Each function must have either a single return value, or two return values of
which the second has type error. In that case, if the second (error)
return value evaluates to non-nil during execution, execution terminates and
Execute returns that error.

Errors returned by Execute wrap the underlying error; call [errors.AsType] to
unwrap them.

When template execution invokes a function with an argument list, that list
must be assignable to the function's parameter types. Functions meant to
apply to arguments of arbitrary type can use parameters of type interface{} or
of type [reflect.Value]. Similarly, functions meant to return a result of arbitrary
type can return interface{} or [reflect.Value].

nodes.Name: builtins
nodes.DocComment:
builtins returns the FuncMap.
It is not a global variable so the linker can dead code eliminate
more when this isn't called. See golang.org/issue/36021.
TODO: revert this back to a global map once golang.org/issue/2559 is fixed.

nodes.Name: builtinFuncs
nodes.DocComment: builtinFuncs lazily computes & caches the builtinFuncs map.

nodes.Name: addValueFuncs
nodes.DocComment: addValueFuncs adds to values the functions in funcs, converting them to reflect.Values.

nodes.Name: addFuncs
nodes.DocComment:
addFuncs adds to values the functions in funcs. It does no checking of the input -
call addValueFuncs first.

nodes.Name: goodFunc
nodes.DocComment: goodFunc reports whether the function or method has the right result signature.

nodes.Name: goodName
nodes.DocComment: goodName reports whether the function name is a valid identifier.

nodes.Name: findFunction
nodes.DocComment: findFunction looks for a function in the template, and global map.

nodes.Name: prepareArg
nodes.DocComment:
prepareArg checks if value can be used as an argument of type argType, and
converts an invalid value to appropriate zero if possible.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: indexArg
nodes.DocComment: indexArg checks if a reflect.Value can be used as an index, and converts it to int if possible.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: index
nodes.DocComment:
index returns the result of indexing its first argument by the following
arguments. Thus "index x 1 2 3" is, in Go syntax, x[1][2][3]. Each
indexed item must be a map, slice, or array.

nodes.Name: slice
nodes.DocComment:
slice returns the result of slicing its first argument by the remaining
arguments. Thus "slice x 1 2" is, in Go syntax, x[1:2], while "slice x"
is x[:], "slice x 1" is x[1:], and "slice x 1 2 3" is x[1:2:3]. The first
argument must be a string, slice, or array.

nodes.Name: length
nodes.DocComment: length returns the length of the item, with an error if it has no defined length.

nodes.Name: call
nodes.DocComment:
call returns the result of evaluating the first argument as a function.
The function must return 1 result, or 2 results, the second of which is an error.

nodes.Name: safeCall
nodes.DocComment:
safeCall runs fun.Call(args), and returns the resulting value and error, if
any. If the call panics, the panic value is returned as an error.

nodes.Name: and
nodes.DocComment:
and computes the Boolean AND of its arguments, returning
the first false argument it encounters, or the last argument.

nodes.Name: or
nodes.DocComment:
or computes the Boolean OR of its arguments, returning
the first true argument it encounters, or the last argument.

nodes.Name: not
nodes.DocComment: not returns the Boolean negation of its argument.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: isNil
nodes.DocComment: isNil returns true if v is the zero reflect.Value, or nil of its type.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Chan, reflect.Func, reflect.Interface, reflect.Map, reflect.Pointer, reflect.Slice

nodes.Name: canCompare
nodes.DocComment:
canCompare reports whether v1 and v2 are both the same kind, or one is nil.
Called only when dealing with nillable types, or there's about to be an error.

nodes.Name: eq
nodes.DocComment: eq evaluates the comparison a == b || a == c || ...

nodes.Name: ne
nodes.DocComment: ne evaluates the comparison a != b.

nodes.Name: lt
nodes.DocComment: lt evaluates the comparison a < b.

nodes.Name: le
nodes.DocComment: le evaluates the comparison <= b.

nodes.Name: gt
nodes.DocComment: gt evaluates the comparison a > b.

nodes.Name: ge
nodes.DocComment: ge evaluates the comparison a >= b.

nodes.Name: HTMLEscape
nodes.DocComment: HTMLEscape writes to w the escaped HTML equivalent of the plain text data b.

nodes.Name: HTMLEscapeString
nodes.DocComment: HTMLEscapeString returns the escaped HTML equivalent of the plain text data s.

nodes.Name: HTMLEscaper
nodes.DocComment:
HTMLEscaper returns the escaped HTML equivalent of the textual
representation of its arguments.

nodes.Name: JSEscape
nodes.DocComment: JSEscape writes to w the escaped JavaScript equivalent of the plain text data b.

nodes.Name: JSEscapeString
nodes.DocComment: JSEscapeString returns the escaped JavaScript equivalent of the plain text data s.

nodes.Name: JSEscaper
nodes.DocComment:
JSEscaper returns the escaped JavaScript equivalent of the textual
representation of its arguments.

nodes.Name: URLQueryEscaper
nodes.DocComment:
URLQueryEscaper returns the escaped value of the textual representation of
its arguments in a form suitable for embedding in a URL query.

nodes.Name: evalArgs
nodes.DocComment:
evalArgs formats the list of arguments into a string. It is therefore equivalent to

	fmt.Sprint(args...)

except that each argument is indirected (if a pointer), as required,
using the same rules as the default string evaluation during template
execution.
